hypotheses.hypothesis: Killing the single checkoutservice pod will cause the place-order workflow to fail because checkoutservice is a critical synchronous dependency in the order path.
hypotheses.weakness_surface: Single replica of checkoutservice; no redundancy; synchronous call from frontend to checkoutservice.
hypotheses.expected_invariant: frontend HTTP 200 and successful order response with order_id and shipping_tracking_id
hypotheses.validation_plan: baseline, inject, observe, recover, cleanup, washout
hypotheses.recovery_expectation: After pod restart, checkoutservice becomes available and the workflow succeeds again.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Killing the frontend pod will cause the health check to fail and the entire workflow to be unavailable.
hypotheses.weakness_surface: Single replica of frontend; no redundancy; frontend is the entry point for both health check and order workflow.
hypotheses.expected_invariant: frontend HTTP 200 and successful order response with order_id and shipping_tracking_id
hypotheses.validation_plan: baseline, inject, observe, recover, cleanup, washout
hypotheses.recovery_expectation: After frontend pod restarts, health check and order workflow succeed again.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Killing the cartservice pod will cause the AddItem step to fail, preventing the order workflow from completing.
hypotheses.weakness_surface: Single replica of cartservice; cartservice is a synchronous dependency for adding items to cart.
hypotheses.expected_invariant: frontend HTTP 200 and successful order response with order_id and shipping_tracking_id
hypotheses.validation_plan: baseline, inject, observe, recover, cleanup, washout
hypotheses.recovery_expectation: After cartservice pod restarts, AddItem and PlaceOrder succeed again.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Introducing 500ms latency to checkoutservice will cause timeouts in the order workflow, leading to failure.
hypotheses.weakness_surface: Synchronous call to checkoutservice; no explicit timeout/retry evidence; high latency may exceed client timeout.
hypotheses.expected_invariant: frontend HTTP 200 and successful order response with order_id and shipping_tracking_id
hypotheses.validation_plan: baseline, inject, observe, recover, cleanup, washout
hypotheses.recovery_expectation: After latency injection stops, checkoutservice responds normally and workflow succeeds.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Introducing 50% packet loss to checkoutservice will cause intermittent failures in the order workflow, likely leading to failure.
hypotheses.weakness_surface: Synchronous call to checkoutservice; packet loss may cause connection errors or timeouts.
hypotheses.expected_invariant: frontend HTTP 200 and successful order response with order_id and shipping_tracking_id
hypotheses.validation_plan: baseline, inject, observe, recover, cleanup, washout
hypotheses.recovery_expectation: After loss injection stops, checkoutservice becomes reliable and workflow succeeds.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Stressing the frontend CPU to 80% will cause the health check to become slow or fail, impacting the workflow.
hypotheses.weakness_surface: Frontend is the entry point; CPU starvation may cause timeouts on health and order requests.
hypotheses.expected_invariant: frontend HTTP 200 and successful order response with order_id and shipping_tracking_id
hypotheses.validation_plan: baseline, inject, observe, recover, cleanup, washout
hypotheses.recovery_expectation: After CPU stress stops, frontend recovers and workflow succeeds.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Introducing 500ms latency to cartservice will cause the AddItem step to time out, preventing order placement.
hypotheses.weakness_surface: Synchronous call to cartservice; no explicit timeout/retry evidence; high latency may exceed client timeout.
hypotheses.expected_invariant: frontend HTTP 200 and successful order response with order_id and shipping_tracking_id
hypotheses.validation_plan: baseline, inject, observe, recover, cleanup, washout
hypotheses.recovery_expectation: After latency injection stops, cartservice responds normally and workflow succeeds.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Introducing 50% packet loss to cartservice will cause the AddItem step to fail intermittently, likely preventing order placement.
hypotheses.weakness_surface: Synchronous call to cartservice; packet loss may cause connection errors or timeouts.
hypotheses.expected_invariant: frontend HTTP 200 and successful order response with order_id and shipping_tracking_id
hypotheses.validation_plan: baseline, inject, observe, recover, cleanup, washout
hypotheses.recovery_expectation: After loss injection stops, cartservice becomes reliable and workflow succeeds.
